change: G2 repair: D1 -- fixed reconstruct_poc_va_nodes() padding from the occupied-weight range instead of the window's bar range (win_lo_tick/win_hi_tick), which silently shifted vah/val for allocation=close. D2a -- exact_triplets persisted only on the rare snapshot where the live kernel's own walk took the exact re-decision path. D2b -- profile_json (JSON text) replaced by profile: a typed struct field (BaseBinding.FIELD_TYPES, a generic platform mechanism), carried through the host sink/parquet as a typed Arrow struct with flat list<int64> children, never JSON text.
oracle: the kernel's own live scalar snapshot (poc, vah, val, va_weight_fraction, raw_poc, raw_vah, raw_val, n_hvn, n_lvn, hvns_json, lvns_json); VolumeProfileSnapshot.reconstruct_poc_va_nodes must reproduce it bit for bit from weights_fp/contributions/exact_triplets (via from_struct()) alone, AFTER a real ColumnarBuffer -> to_frame -> to_parquet -> read_parquet round trip (not merely an in-process JSON round trip).
method: real tape, two 4-day windows picked by raw bar volume (never by outcomes): 2022-02-01..04 (baseline) and 2022-10-11..14 (2022-10-13, the September CPI print release day, is the 3rd highest single-day bar-volume day of 2022). Every closed-minute snapshot (not sampled) for all 3 allocations x {120, 360, 1440} horizons is flushed through research_workflow.host.sink.ColumnarBuffer, written to parquet, read back, and reconstructed. scripts/parity_volume_profile_rolling_profile_emission.py.
criterion: zero mismatches on poc/vah/val/raw_poc/raw_vah/raw_val/n_hvn/n_lvn/hvns_json/lvns_json, bit-exact weights_fp/contributions, and a matching content_hash, across every one of 98,838 checked snapshots (2 windows x 3 allocations x 3 horizons x 5491 snapshots each).

full_year_extrapolation.note: lifecycle_v2.run_partition holds the WHOLE partition's candidate/observation rows as plain Python objects (ColumnarBuffer lists of dicts, no numpy/arrow backing) until a SINGLE to_parquet() flush at partition end -- no incremental/chunked flush exists today. The on-disk (parquet, typed Arrow) footprint is comfortably within the 8 GiB budget; the in-memory PRE-FLUSH Python-object footprint is not, because of CPython per-object overhead on the profile struct's weights_fp/contributions int lists, not because of the serialized representation itself.

redundancy_note: mean fraction of weight-vector bins UNCHANGED minute-to-minute ranges ~0.82 (120 min horizon) to ~0.97 (1440 min horizon) across allocations (see windows.<baseline>.<alloc>/<h>.redundancy); a delta encoding (changed-bin index + value, 16 bytes/changed bin) would be roughly 5-33% of the full vector's raw byte size depending on horizon/allocation -- analysis only, not implemented (would require a normalized/immutable-profile-reference or delta-chain representation, a platform capability decision, not a bug repair).
not_done: D2(5) redundancy analysis is numbers-only, not implemented (a delta/normalized-reference representation is a platform capability decision). The full-year in-memory peak (~126 GiB projected for 9 kernels over 354,135 open minutes) exceeds the ~8 GiB per-partition budget even after D1/D2a/D2b: the blocker is lifecycle_v2.run_partition's own buffering (the WHOLE partition's rows held as plain Python objects, no numpy/arrow backing, until a single to_parquet() flush at partition end -- there is no incremental/chunked flush today), not the representation (on-disk projected size is ~4.5 GiB/year, comfortably inside budget). Resolving the in-memory blocker needs an incremental-flush change to the host/lifecycle collection path, which is a platform/study-design decision outside this bounded repair.
